sections.title: Where to start
sections.desc: Test, reading the profiles, quick reference points

items.label: Suggested order
items.value: 1) Take the test. 2) Read the dominant type. 3) Check wings + subtype. 4) Observe stress/growth. 5) Use levels 1–9 to place your current state.

items.label: Important
items.value: The test gives a hypothesis. Validation comes from reading the deep motivations (fear/desire) and the mechanisms (passion/fixation/defense).

items.label: Ancient roots
items.value: Origins are debated; possible influences include ancient traditions, the Desert Fathers, Sufism, and the Kabbalah (depending on the school).

children.label: Gurdjieff
children.value: Introduced the symbol to the West (the Law of Three and of Seven), but not yet the 9 types.

children.label: Ichazo
children.value: Placed the fixations on the symbol (Arica school).

children.label: Naranjo
children.value: Connected it to character/modern psychology, developed the panels.

items.label: Definition
items.value: Instinctive center (body/action), emotional center (heart/image/relationships), mental center (head/analysis/security).

sections.title: Wings, subtypes, arrows
sections.desc: Nuances of the type + stress/growth movements

items.label: Wings
items.value: The two neighboring types influence the base type (one wing is often dominant).

items.label: Arrows
items.value: Under stress and in growth, we adopt traits of other types; these describe tendencies, not an identity.

sections.title: Levels 1–9
sections.desc: From the most free to the most automatic + reference points by type

items.label: Quick reading
items.value: 1–3: healthy zone. 4–6: average zone. 7–9: unhealthy zone. The type doesn't change, but the degree of identification does.

sections.title: Practices for transformation
sections.desc: Observing, journaling, meditation, inquiry, the body

items.label: Inner observer
items.value: Catching the automatism as it happens (catching yourself in the act), without judgment or justification.

items.label: Journaling
items.value: Note triggers, reactions, the fear/desire behind the action; reread at the end of the day.

children.label: Vipassana
children.value: Observing sensations/thoughts without clinging to them.

items.label: Inquiry (Diamond Approach)
items.value: Exploring present experience with curiosity, without wanting to change it, until contact with an essential quality.

items.label: Bodywork
items.value: Returning to the body (breathing, grounding, gentle movement) to step out of the mental/emotional trance.
